clue.text: This may be an advantage when one is in court

definitions.text: This may be an advantage when one is in court

parts.words: an advantage when one is in court
parts.note: surface reading: a legal edge enjoyed by someone facing a judge
setter's reading: on a tennis court, where 'advantage' is a scoring term and one more point wins the game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'advantage' both suggest a lawsuit, but in tennis 'advantage' is the score after deuce, when the leading player needs only one more point.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the stage where the server or receiver needs just a single further rally to win the game carries this name.

clue.text: The opposite of a long after-dinner speech?

definitions.text: The opposite of a long after-dinner speech?

parts.note: surface reading: a rambling toast delivered once the meal is over
setter's reading: reverse each part, giving a short speech before dinner, the prayer said at table

explanation.walkthrough: Flip 'long' to short and 'after' to before: a short before-dinner speech is the brief prayer of thanks said at the start of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The prayer of thanks offered at table before eating is traditionally brief, the reverse of a lengthy speech following the meal.

clue.text: Part of vehicle showing dirt — panic!

parts.note: wet dirt is mud
to be in a flap is to be in a panic

explanation.surface: A driver panics at the sight of a filthy car part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' is informal British for a state of agitation or panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber guard hung behind a wheel to stop spray and stones flying up is a component fitted to cars and lorries.

clue.text: Puppet hit the drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the hook-nosed glove puppet who beats Judy in seaside shows
second meaning: to strike with the fist
third meaning: a mixed bowl of fruit juice and spirits

explanation.surface: A puppet takes to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row: 'hit the drink' reads as a phrase but splits into a verb and a noun. Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the famous glove puppet, a blow with the fist, and a party beverage served from a bowl.

clue.text: I shall twice hide whiskey, out of spite

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it out of sight inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: I shall contracts to I'll, written twice
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone vows to hide the whiskey twice over, purely out of malice.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in I'll is dropped, as crosswords allow, and W sits between the two copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice or hostile feeling toward another person is a close synonym of spite.

clue.text: Difficulty getting undergarment to reach stomach

parts.note: tights are a close-fitting leg garment
a pot, as in pot belly, is a round stomach

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to pull underwear up over their belly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a garment stretched to the waist; the answer splits after the S of the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in an awkward predicament with little room to escape is an idiom for trouble or hardship.

clue.text: Into mug, start to spit part of tooth

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside, so a letter goes within the vessel

parts.note: a mug is a kind of drinking cup

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of spit

explanation.surface: At the dentist, a patient spits a bit of broken tooth into a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards from the usual order: the instruction comes first and the definition last.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed projections on the chewing surface of molars are what dentists call these, a technical anatomical term.

clue.text: Infectious disease? Arrest her, is the call

indicators.note: a call is something shouted out, so what matters is how the words are pronounced

parts.note: to collar someone is slang for arresting them

explanation.surface: A police officer, fearing contagion, shouts orders to detain a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' is informal for arrest, so the cry 'Collar her!' is pronounced like the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacterial illness spread through contaminated water, causing severe diarrhoea, is a classic example of a contagious ailment.

clue.text: Batman say may be out of our sphere

indicators.note: something out of place is disordered, so these letters leave their arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Batman, perhaps, belongs to a world beyond ours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Batman as an example of the answer rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The caped crusader of DC Comics is a prime instance of a costumed crimefighter with special powers or gadgets.

clue.text: Churchman's ticket home to Alabama

parts.note: a card can be a ticket, as in a membership card
someone at home is in
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: A clergyman holds his ticket back to Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is' joining definition to wordplay; 'home' gives IN, as in staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior prelate of the Roman Catholic Church, entitled to elect the Pope, is a high-ranking cleric.

clue.text: Gatherings of heartless adults

indicators.note: without a heart means the central part is cut out

parts.note: adults are grown-ups

explanation.surface: Meetings of cold, uncaring grown-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters, WN, are removed from GROWNUPS, leaving GROUPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of people who come together are assemblies, clusters or bands, all close synonyms.

clue.text: Left in high temperature, hot toast

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit within it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: heat is high temperature
L is the standard abbreviation for left
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Bread left in high heat becomes hot toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot toast' looks like breakfast; toast is the definition in its drinking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a glass and saying 'Your health!' is a classic way of proposing a drink in someone's honour.

clue.text: Supposedly popular assumption

parts.note: what is in is fashionable or popular
a theory is a supposition or assumption

explanation.surface: A widely held belief, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first; the rest is a two-part charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something holds on paper but perhaps not in practice is an adverbial phrase meaning allegedly or ostensibly.

clue.text: Dick parking in Italian city

indicators.note: being in a place means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A man named Dick is parking his car in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick is not a common noun but a first name: Dick Turpin was a notorious 18th-century English highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous English robber's first name was Dick, so the given name defines his surname in crossword style.

clue.text: Pad raised armrest?

parts.note: something raised is up
read as arm rest: a holster is where a firearm rests

explanation.surface: A cushioned arm on a chair is lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armrest' looks like part of a chair, apt for padding, but it splits as arm, a weapon, and rest, its resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit stuffing, springs and covering to furniture is to cushion it, a verb meaning to fill with soft material.

clue.text: Top-ranked tennis player, small and quiet

parts.note: top-ranked is number one, written NO I
Monica Seles, former world number one tennis player
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: The world's best tennis player is petite and reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top-ranked tennis player' reads as one phrase, but splits into number one (NO I) and Seles, who was world number one in the early 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Making no sound at all is silent or hushed, synonyms of the adjective.

clue.text: Stride along and dare to jump about like a bloodhound

parts.note: to lope is to run with long easy strides

indicators.note: jumping about means moving around in a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog bounds along and leaps around, as a bloodhound would.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the bloodhound the one striding and jumping, but its long drooping ears are the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodhounds have long hanging ears that droop down, which is what having floppy dangling ears describes.

clue.text: Enormous wife going on one leg

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
hopping is moving on one leg

explanation.surface: A huge woman balancing on a single leg.
explanation.walkthrough: W for wife is a standard abbreviation, as in genealogies.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial adjective for something huge or very large in size is a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Ref's decision may be fine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a kick awarded by the referee in football
second meaning: a sum paid as punishment

explanation.surface: A referee's ruling might be perfectly acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like approval of the decision, but it is the monetary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee awarding a spot kick is giving one, and a monetary punishment is another sense of the same noun.

clue.text: Understand our team will recover

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
our team is we, and we will contracts to we'll

explanation.surface: A fan insists that the struggling side will bounce back.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of we'll is dropped, as crosswords allow.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain health after illness is a phrasal verb meaning to recuperate.

clue.text: Excellent from end of tail to head

parts.note: the tip is the end of a tail
the head of something is its top

explanation.surface: Splendid from one end of the animal to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From tail to head' suggests reading backwards, but it simply places one end before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal adjective for first-rate or of the highest quality is a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: On plate, toyed with mush

indicators.note: something toyed with is played around with, so these letters are messed about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fussy diner pushes porridge around the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Polenta is an Italian dish of boiled cornmeal, served soft or set.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiled maize meal cooked to a soft porridge is a kind of pulp or soft food, a fair example of the word.

clue.text: Aircraft finally cancelled, chap sounding mournful

indicators.note: the final part being cancelled means the last letter is struck off

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A man laments when his flight is called off at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounding mournful' looks like it describes the chap, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud, resonant and melancholy tone, like a tolling bell, is what this literary adjective describes.

clue.text: Religiously set aside as hard to let

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A church property kept off the rental market as it is hard to let.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to let' looks like a property hard to rent out; it is H followed by a synonym for let.
explanation.definitionFit: To make or consecrate something as sacred is to dedicate it for holy purposes, as in 'hallowed be thy name'.

clue.text: Felt revulsion for wrong order for death

indicators.note: putting things in the wrong order means mixing up their sequence

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at the idea of an execution warrant made out wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong order for death' sounds like a misissued death warrant; the definition is the opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling intense loathing or disgust toward something is to have detested it, a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Premonitions women silently suppress

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down out of view, so the letters are kept within

parts.note: inside the two words

explanation.surface: Women keep their forebodings to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of the two words: wOMEN Silently.
explanation.definitionFit: Signs foretelling the future, good or bad, are portents, close in sense to forebodings.

clue.text: Follower of Churchill emerges from battle, exhausted

indicators.note: something that emerges from a thing was inside it, so the letters come out of the words

parts.note: inside the two words

explanation.surface: A wartime supporter of Churchill staggers out of the fight, worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follower' suggests a supporter, but Clement Attlee succeeded Churchill as British Prime Minister in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour leader who became Prime Minister after the 1945 election came after Churchill in office.

clue.text: Holy book, short, was liable to be made longer

parts.note: Ex is the short form of Exodus, a book of the Bible
if something tended to happen, it was liable to

explanation.surface: A short scripture was likely to be lengthened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' makes the book's name brief: Ex. is the standard abbreviation for Exodus.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthened or stretched out in duration or size is a past participle meaning prolonged.

clue.text: Old city that attracted ten years of investment

definitions.text: Old city that attracted ten years of investment

parts.note: surface reading: a place that drew a decade of financial backing
setter's reading: investment is also a siege, and the Greeks besieged this ancient city for ten years

explanation.walkthrough: To invest a city is an old military term for surrounding it; the Trojan War siege lasted ten years.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient city of Homer's Iliad, besieged by the Greeks for a decade, fits the old city described.

clue.text: Vegetarian period of Cleopatra's youth

parts.note: surface reading: a time when someone ate no meat
setter's reading: Shakespeare's Cleopatra calls her inexperienced youth the time when she was green in judgment

explanation.walkthrough: In Antony and Cleopatra she speaks of 'My salad days, when I was green in judgment', the source of the phrase for youthful inexperience.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for one's time of youthful innocence and naivety comes from Shakespeare's Egyptian queen, and leafy greens suggest vegetarianism.
